speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor

That facial rash sparing the area around the mouth is very characteristic; did you also notice any swelling or redness in her hands or feet? Additionally, has she had any abdominal pain or vomiting recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease) caused by Parvovirus B19.

The combination of a recent viral prodrome (fever, headache, rhinorrhea) followed by a pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities, along with a characteristic facial rash that spares the perioral area, is classic for this condition. While the CBC results would likely show reticulocytopenia, the clinical presentation is highly specific and does not require further testing for confirmation.
